items.rationale: Sections 2.4.2 and 5.2.6 cover reinstatement of the water-damaged panel, including the plinth wrap. Allow €90/m² for 3 m² of small-area installation, excluding the tiles billed separately.
The single opening for the existing pipe is necessary making good under §5.2.6. Allow €70 for the drilling service if it is not already included in the tile installation rate.
Sections 3.5(a) and 7.1.6 limit replacement to comparable budget-grade white tiles. Allow 3 m² at €18/m².
Sections 5.2.6 and 7.1.5 cover rebuilding the documented soft patch, not levelling the whole panel. Allow €22 in material for the 1 m² patch.
The standard tiles on line 3 already cover the damaged panel. Sections 3.5(a), (d) and (e) bar a second allowance for unnecessary oversize tiles; €54 is the conditional standard-grade benchmark.
Sections 5.2.6 and 7.1.5 cover silicone at the wall-to-plinth junction and the side-wall termination, not the grouted edges. The described dimensions support about 3.3 m at €14/m.

Sections 3.5(a), (d) and (e) exclude the premium uplift, overlap with line 6 and unsupported extra length. If materials are shown to be separate from line 6, allow €12 for ordinary sealant for the documented joints only.
Section 7.4.2 permits the first travel charge on the tiler's invoice. Apply the calibrated €80 allowance for one charge.

Section 7.4.1 bars separate hours for work already priced in unit rates or lump sums, and §3.5(b) excludes attic work. The conditional €599 estimate is 14 hours at the reference rate of about €43/hour, payable only if those hours are shown to be distinct, necessary cellar work.

Section 3.5(c) allows cleaning of reinstated surfaces as part of the repair, but §§7.4.1 and 7.4.4 do not support billing an ordinary finishing wipe twice. Allow €25 only if a distinct necessary cleaning service is substantiated.
Sections 5.2.1 and 5.2.6 cover dismantling the wet meter boxing. Allow €85 for removal only, excluding container disposal and any future refitting.

items.description: Remove and dispose of wet boxing insulation
items.rationale: Section 5.2.1 covers the wet mineral wool removed from the boxing and separately taken away by the tiler. Allow €74 for one charge; it is distinct from both the container debris and the pipe lagging removed by the owner.
Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.5 cover removal of the damp render behind the affected panel, with no allowance for other cellar areas. Allow 3 m² at €35/m², excluding container disposal.
Sections 2.4.2 and 3.5(b) exclude the unrelated attic work: the staining predates the cellar leak. The €90 figure is a conditional benchmark for a small removal job, not an allowance for this loss.
Section 5.2.6 covers like-for-like replacement of the cover ring that cracked during necessary tile removal. Allow €12 for one ordinary chrome rosette.

Section 2.4.2 covers the resulting water damage, but §2.4.3 does not establish fracture cover for a sound nut with a failed olive. If distinct access or refitting work is substantiated under §5.2.6, one short service is worth about €65.
Section 5.2.7 covers the seven days supported by moisture readings, not the later precautionary use of the owner's machine. Allow €126 at €18/day for one construction dryer.

Sections 7.4.3 and 7.4.4 require a surcharge to be tied to necessary materials rather than overhead, duplicate supplies or materials for an uncovered joint repair. A substantiated minor reinstatement consumables charge would be about €12.
Sections 2.4.2 and 7.1.6 cover like-for-like replacement of the metre of lagging soaked by the escape. Apply the reference allowance of €22 for 1 m.
Section 5.2.1 covers one disposal charge for the actual tile, render and board debris. This is separate from the mineral wool taken away by the tiler; allow the calibrated €60 flat rate.
